hook: Ten families graze cattle on one open pasture. It feeds 100 cows well. One family adds an eleventh cow: it keeps the whole value of that cow, while the grass the cow eats is lost to all ten families. Every family does the same math, the pasture is grazed bare, and soon it feeds far fewer cows than before.

options: The largest population an environment can support over time
The fastest rate a population can grow
The number of species in an ecosystem
The total biomass of the producers
prereq.why: Carrying capacity is the largest population the resources of an environment can support for a long time.

prereq.q: Fish caught for food from the ocean are an example of which ecosystem service?
prereq.why: Provisioning services are the goods people take from ecosystems: food, water, wood and fiber.

figure.caption: One herder keeps all of the gain from an extra cow but pays only a share of the cost, so every herder adds cows and the shared pasture runs down.

chain.cause: A resource is open to everyone and owned by no one
chain.effect: no single user has a reason to protect it

chain.cause: Each user keeps the full gain from taking more while the cost is shared
Total use rises above what the resource can renew
chain.effect: the resource shrinks, so each user gets less

chain.cause: Rules that limit or assign use (permits, quotas, fees, community agreements)
chain.effect: use falls back to what the resource can renew

ideas: A common resource is shared, hard to fence off, and used up as it is used: open pastures, ocean fisheries, aquifers, the air.
The tragedy of the commons is not about bad people. Each user acts sensibly for themselves; together they run the resource down.
The gain from taking more goes to one user; the cost is split among all users. That gap is the cause.
Fixes change the rewards: limits set by law (permits, quotas, seasons), fees for use, private or assigned rights, or community rules with monitoring and penalties.

misconception.wrong: The tragedy of the commons happens because users do not know they are harming the resource.
misconception.right: Users can know the resource is shrinking and still take more, because each one keeps the whole gain from taking more but pays only a small share of the loss. Rules that change those rewards fix it; information alone often does not.

summary: A shared resource that no one controls is overused because each user gains in full from taking more while the cost is spread over everyone. Pastures, fisheries, aquifers and the atmosphere all show it. Solutions change the rewards: limits set by law, fees, assigned rights, or community rules with monitoring.
